releases.name: spaCR 1.5.1.5
releases.body:
**macOS:** install with `spaCR-1.5.1.5-macOS-Universal-Online.pkg`. The standalone `.dmg` will be added to this release once its launch check passes.

## spaCR 1.5.1.5

### Upgrading

On macOS, how to reach 1.5.1.5 depends on the version you have:

- 1.5.0.8, 1.5.0.9 and 1.5.1.0: install the 1.5.1.5 `.pkg` from the [releases page](https://github.com/EinarOlafsson/spacr/releases). Do not use Help > Check for updates: the updater in these versions removes the user runtime and then stops before installing. The `.pkg` restores a working installation.
- 1.5.0.1: install the `.pkg`. Its in-app update cannot run.
- 1.5.0.4 to 1.5.0.7 and 1.5.1.2 to 1.5.1.4: Help > Check for updates works. On an Intel Mac, an update that lands on 1.5.1.4 reports "Numpy is not available"; updating to 1.5.1.5 repairs it.

On every platform, a new install of 1.5.1.3 or 1.5.1.4, or an update to either, now installs PySide6 6.12.0, which can crash spaCR. 1.5.1.5 excludes 6.12.0, so updating to 1.5.1.5 replaces it.

### New

- Make Masks opens 3D images in the same view as 2D ones. A slice slider and the Z wheel move through the stack, and the view can be Default, Orthogonal or True 3D. Draw and edit masks on any slice and delete objects; edited volumes are saved as whole sections.
- Make Masks supports transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images.
- A FIB-SEM example volume with 3D mitochondria masks (EMPIAR-10982, HeLa, CC0). Fetch it with `spacr-download fibsem`.
- Export settings... on every settings form, and Save settings CSV... in Distributed Jobs (#140, #141, #142).
- Preferences > Appearance > Accessibility: High contrast, Text size, Reduce motion, Stronger focus outlines and Keyboard shortcuts.
- Startup uses one borderless window that opens at screen size. The spaCR logo, built from microscopy tiles, holds for 2 s and then breaks apart over 4 s. Help has a replay entry. The other startup dialogs (drafts, installer consent, tour, What's new) wait until the sequence ends or is skipped.
- Gate Editor: the mode, plane and spin keys can be rebound, and a picker lets you choose between overlapping elements.
- Model Zoo has a model card viewer with three pages (scores, training facts, about). Cards download from Hugging Face, are cached, and fall back to the bundled card when offline.
- `spacr-tutorial` opens the online tutorials.
- Object detection has a 3D switch. When on, 3D thresholds are used, and Cellpose runs in 3D or stitches 2D slices into 3D objects.
- Make Masks measures the current 3D image.
- Make Masks has an Edit Label action and a Time button. +Cell and +Daughter record division lineage, which is stored in 32-bit TIFF masks.
- Anonymous error reports can be sent without a GitHub account. They are on by default and can be turned off in Preferences. spaCR AI is available to help with errors.
- Updates download and stage in the background and ask once to Restart. Preferences > Performance > Uninstall... removes the current version or all versions.
- Submit to cluster reads your `~/.ssh` config and handles logins that need a second factor.
- Plaque model toxoplasma_plaque_v5.

### Improved

- Updates stage replacement runtimes, check downloaded installers and verify the requested installed version before relaunch. User data and configured model/cache folders are protected; optional cleanup is off by default and offers a graphical folder preview. For the first upgrade from an older frozen Windows installation, use the new desktop installer before relying on the new in-app update path.
- Saved workspaces retain selected databases, montage and graph settings, regression views and queued figures. Copied references are verified before restoration.
- Installer and mask-editing messages are refreshed across the nine interface languages.
- The well detector v3 is the default in the app, the README and the model cards. The plaque default is toxoplasma_plaque_v5; v3 is recommended for Gel Doc wells.
- Model cards use the ground-truth re-score of 2026-10-11 (object F1, precision, recall, AJI, Dice, with stock Cellpose-SAM for comparison). The README shows one score card per model.
- Sixteen settings that accept a fixed list are now dropdowns, for example `spatial_platform`. Stored values are unchanged.
- Regression: `dependent_variable` is a dropdown of the numeric columns in the score file, with a note when `pred` is missing (#144).
- Measure reads a pasted list of plate folders as plates (#138, #139).
- Classify: relative database paths in `src` work, and a missing database is reported with the full path searched (#143).
- Mixed model: Stop is reported as a stop, the nested design is checked before the fit with the setting to change named, and optimiser fallbacks are handled (#145).
- Magnification sets the default Cellpose diameter. A diameter of 0 and "auto" are the same.
- Make Masks: each disconnected brush stroke is a new object. Hold Shift to continue an object across gaps; hold Alt to pan.
- Accessibility names now cover lists, the main window and Preferences.
- Wording in the app, docs and API is factual and reviewed in nine languages, and settings section titles are translated.
- The GUI no longer freezes during the Regression example download and batch run, and Regression results open faster on first use.
- Pages with folds open faster the first time.
- Preference reads are kept open instead of being reopened.
- Invasion and other long analyses no longer starve the GUI, because garbage collection is deferred to idle time.
- Plate View applies only the newest recompute.
- Mask screens render their field backgrounds more efficiently.
- Preferences opens, applies and closes faster, and Apply, Keep and Revert no longer freeze the app.
- Make Masks costs less per frame.
- Make Masks timelapse: the Track preview keeps each frame's pictures, so scrubbing and playback no longer slow the window, and zoom and pan stay put while the movie plays.
- Curate keeps its picture between repaints and redraws only the area a brush stroke changes.
- The Methods & Results page and Regression open faster; the libraries they need are loaded in the background at startup.
- Dropping a large folder on Make Masks keeps the window responsive: the folder is walked faster, and the report, regex editor and metadata table are built in small steps.
- Switching between Essentials and All settings no longer pauses the app while the choice is saved.
- Every saved mask records its field's size, and a mask of a different size is never reused.
- The README is rebuilt from images, and the slide deck is rebuilt to match. README and interface text are translated into nine languages.
- Apptainer (SIF) images are published with each release, after the Docker images.

### Fixed

- The OpenGL 3D renderer works on a fresh install: spaCR now installs PyOpenGL, and the Render backend list offers OpenGL only when it can import, so the view no longer silently falls back to the CPU.
- Mask generation keeps the raw images by default: `keep_original_images` now defaults to True (with `save_original_images`), so orig/ is no longer deleted when a run finishes. Set it to False to discard them; the log then says how many raw images are removed (issue #154).
- Closing the main window saves pending Annotate labels and drains its page loader and database writer.
- Corrected the restart command and launch environment for frozen desktop applications, while preserving saved workspace state.
- Prevented environment capture from relaunching frozen desktop applications.
- Installations avoid PySide6 6.12.0, which can crash rendering on Python 3.10.
- Failed cache moves retain data and location settings, restore an existing empty destination after successful rollback, and do not broaden its permissions.
- Own-DINO classifier loading rejects teacher checkpoints that change during loading.
- Embeddings reports unreadable or empty label tables without discarding existing labels, vectors or scorecards.
- Resizable panes keep their remembered sizes and close safely with their screen.
- Figures restored from a saved workspace retain thumbnail detail on high-DPI screens.
- Module screens no longer stall every 2 s. The GPU is read through NVML instead of starting `nvidia-smi`, and usage bars paint with the next frame.
- Command palette: a key typed while the list is rebuilding is kept instead of crashing the app.
- Regression panel: fixed a thread error.
- Legacy PNG masks load in Make Masks.
- The workspace is saved on the GUI thread.
- Text is re-measured after a font change.
- Make Masks: a linked image with no box ledger opens and saves without the "Cannot load box annotations" popup.
- A source checkout or editable install reports its own version.
- Wells named F01, F02 are read as wells, and class counts ignore the `.spacr_crop_format.json` file.
- Fixed crashes after Delete selected in Curate's track list and when choosing a folder in Data Manager. Lists, tables and trees now reuse their rows when they redraw.
- Fixed a crash during garbage collection after the first job of a session.
- Installer: an interrupted install no longer blocks later installs as "already running". A lock is taken over only when its installer is provably gone, including the rest of its process group on macOS and Linux and the processes it started on Windows. The message names the lock and the process that holds it, in every installer language.

### Alpha

These appear only with Show alpha features on.

- Own-DINO classifiers can be trained from a supplied teacher checkpoint and applied from their saved artifacts, using explicit channel order and saved input scaling. Predictions and features can be exported as tables.
- MitoNet as a Make Masks backend for TEM images.
- Spatial Mask Generation and Spatial Map Barcodes submodules, opened from the Spatial switches.
- Embeddings offer DINOv2 and can use an official Cell-DINO checkpoint with explicit channel mapping.
- Other organisms stay behind Show alpha species; Toxoplasma is always shown.

releases.name: spaCR 1.5.0.5
releases.body:
spaCR 1.5.0.5 — 7,517 commits and 6,957 files since 1.5.0.4, with 115 new modules and 15 new module screens.

## Main features

**One Qt application, and the old GUI is retired.** The tkinter windows are gone, along with the five standalone launchers (`mask`, `measure`, `make_masks`, `annotate`, `classify`) — every one of them is a tab in the single `spacr` window now, and `spacr-run <module>` is the headless route. The Qt package grew from 180 files to 301.

**Fifteen new module screens.** Regression; Volcano Explorer, which opens a finished regression and lets you interrogate the plot; Image UMAP with Image Scatter and PCA views; Classify with an activation-map workflow embedded in it; Measure; Mask; Map Barcodes with barcode QC; Train Cellpose, which fine-tunes and applies a model in one place; Parameter Sweep, which varies regression settings and shows you which ones change the answer; Model Explanation; Investigate Hit; and Image Import.

**The interface speaks ten languages.** English, Svenska, Deutsch, Español, 简体中文, Português, हिन्दी, 한국어, Íslenska and Français — menus, settings, tooltips and module descriptions, with the README translated alongside.

**A regression suite rather than a single function.** Thirteen modules now cover regression families and their statistical assumptions, alternative backends, effect-size thresholds, panels, layout, search, and failure reporting — including diagnostics whose job is to say whether a screen regression can be believed at all. alpha-RRA aggregates guide-level scores into gene-level calls.

**Native online installers for Linux, Windows and macOS.** Small web installers that build a private environment, pick the right torch backend for the machine, and never ask the user to have a system Python.

**A napari bridge for mask correction.** Hand a field's image and label mask to napari, correct it by hand, and bring the corrected labels back — written the way spaCR writes masks and recorded in the same curation ledger the brush uses. Available headless as `spacr.napari_bridge.correct_mask`.

**The published example screen, in one click.** Download, validation and caching of the TSG101 example data, with `spacr.sra` to fetch the sequencing reads straight from ENA/NCBI.

**Segmentation scorecards.** Score a segmentation against ground truth — which nothing in spaCR could do before — so a model can be published with its numbers beside it.

## Minor features

- **Settings advisor** — inspects the screen's own tables and proposes regression settings, rather than leaving them to be guessed.
- **Label suggestions** — turns a retrained model's scores into labels you can accept or throw away.
- **Gate library** — named gating strategies saved with the project instead of in a file dialog.
- **Workspace save and restore** — the interactive workspace belongs to the run, and GUI state survives a forced restart.
- **Accelerator selection** — one answer to what a job should run on and what that device is called.
- **Benchmark and resource log** — measures throughput and memory to recommend a worker count, and reports what spaCR's whole process tree costs while it runs.
- **Annotation power** — estimates which guide assignments a pooled screen can actually support.
- **Classifier quality** — measures classifier performance and corrects observed class fractions.
- **Fraction calibration** — estimates `fraction_threshold` from control-well concordance instead of a default.
- **Cell montage** — pulls the objects behind a regression coefficient into a montage you can look at.
- **Gene facts and UniProt lookup** — what spaCR already knows about a gene, resolved against UniProt and cached.
- **Reproducible UMAP searches** — Image UMAP searches are stored as embedding recipes that can be re-run.
- **Volcano styling as data** — a plot's appearance is a value, not a pile of arguments.
- **A stable scripting API** — `spacr.api` gives lightweight entry points for scripted workflows.
- **28 optional extras**, including napari, anndata, omero, zarr, czi, lif, nd2, trackastra, ultrack, btrack, rapids, directml, pymc, numpyro, glum, pyfixest, gpytorch and zernike.
- **In-app tutorials** with video and narration, localized into the same ten languages.
- **Faster startup** through lazy imports and prewarming of the heavy modules a screen needs.
- **A much larger test suite** — 64,139 tests now run against the package.

## Note for existing users

The standalone per-module commands are gone; open `spacr` and choose the module, or use `spacr-run <module>` for a headless run. Settings files written by earlier versions still load: renamed settings are mapped to their new names, and settings that were removed outright are named as removed rather than silently ignored.

releases.name: spaCR example screen (TSG101)
releases.body:
The example screen spaCR's "Load example data" button fetches: four plates of per-well gRNA read counts and four plates of per-cell classification scores.

Not committed to the repository and not shipped in the wheel — 33 MB has no business in a pip install. `spacr.example_data` downloads these on demand, verifies each against a recorded SHA-256, and caches them under the user's cache directory so a second press costs nothing.

A dedicated tag rather than a version tag, so re-releasing spaCR does not orphan the data and the URL stays valid across versions.

releases.name: spaCR Nature Communications submission
releases.body:
## spaCR v1.3.6

Release accompanying the manuscript *"A pooled image-based CRISPR screen
identifies EAF1 as a T. gondii modulator of ESCRT subversion"*
(Olafsson et al.). This is the archived version of the code used to
produce the analyses reported in that work.

spaCR (**spa**tial phenotype analysis of **CR**ISPR-Cas9 screens) is an
open-source Python framework that links pooled CRISPR-Cas9 perturbations
to single-cell spatial phenotypes. Rather than decoding barcodes inside
imaged cells, spaCR reads phenotypes from images and genotypes from
matched sequencing plates, then recovers gene-level effects by multiple
linear regression on well-level data.

### Pipeline
- **Mask** — object segmentation (cells, nuclei, pathogens, cytoplasm) via Cellpose
- **Measure** — object-level feature extraction and single-cell image cropping to a SQLite database
- **Classify** — spatial phenotype classification with XGBoost (engineered features) or MaxViT (deep learning), including a manual annotation module for building training sets
- **Map Barcodes** — row, column and gRNA barcode mapping from sequencing reads
- **Regression** — gene-level effect size estimation by multiple linear regression

All five modules are available from the command line and through a graphical user interface.

### Links
- Documentation: https://einarolafsson.github.io/spacr/
- Tutorial: https://einarolafsson.github.io/spacr/tutorial/
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/spacr/
- Screen design and power analysis (R): https://github.com/maomlab/spaCRPower
- Preprint: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.08.737057

Licensed under the MIT License. If you use spaCR, please cite the
manuscript above; see `CITATION.cff` for software citation metadata.
